experience.title: Full-Stack AI Engineer
experience.quote: Solo-engineer pace at a startup — propose, build, ship, iterate crazy fast across the whole stack: data pipelines, agents, video generation, all the way to the UI students actually touch.

experience.title: AI Engineer
experience.quote: From 94% to 98% accuracy and ~40% lower latency — every millisecond counts when banks, hospitals, and government agencies depend on your OCR.

experience.title: AI Engineer
experience.quote: First taste of fintech: real-time fraud detection that retrains itself, and an LLM that reads contracts so the ops team doesn't have to.

writing.title: Agentic AI changed what I have to prove before a question ships
writing.excerpt: At Growtrics, the hard part was not making an agent produce more Q&A. It was deciding which answers deserved to exist, at what coverage and cost.

writing.title: Why we re-trained the OCR backbone instead of fine-tuning
writing.excerpt: Fine-tuning looked faster on paper. The mistakes kept returning in exactly the places that mattered.

writing.title: Shipping a Text-to-SQL agent that doesn't hallucinate column names
writing.excerpt: The first version sounded brilliant right up until it invented a field that did not exist. Confidence is cheap when the schema is not watching.

writing.title: From SmartPay to GMO: 18 months of AI engineering in Vietnam
writing.excerpt: Eighteen months is not enough time to become wise. It is enough time to lose a few illusions about speed, certainty, and what good engineering feels like up close.

writing.title: What 40% latency looks like when a bank is your customer
writing.excerpt: Latency sounds abstract until someone on the customer call starts counting the seconds out loud. Then it becomes a feeling in your chest.
